subject: Next steps: deployment mode & data custody clarifications for FinSecure
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <emartinez@finsecure.com>, Rajiv Patel <rpatel@finsecure.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + ask: deployment mode & data custody clarifications

Thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap from our call and a few clarifying questions so we can size the right path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem).

Key points I captured:
- Primary requirement: all customer PII and transaction logs must be logically isolated from other tenants and retained for 7 years for audit.
- Security wants customer-managed keys (BYOK) for model logs and payload storage; control-plane metadata preferably resident in the US.
- Ops noted: a short POC (2–3 weeks) to validate latency and KV-cache behavior under your traffic profile.

Clarifying questions (can you confirm by EOD Wednesday?):
1) Is there a hard policy that no customer data may co-reside on the same GPU host as other customers (physical isolation), or is logical isolation with encryption + access controls acceptable?
2) Do you require on-premises deployment for any environments (prod vs staging), or will an isolated VPC (Private deployment) suffice?
3) Any specific network egress restrictions (e.g., no public internet calls from inference nodes)?

Next steps from our side once we hear back:
- Nikhil will prepare a short technical note outlining how Redwood Dedicated vs Private VPC meet each ask, including any gaps.
- I27ll share a draft mutual action plan and estimate delta for Dedicated vs Private (including engineering onboarding).
- We can schedule a 30-min deep-dive with your security/infra folks to walk the design.

Attachments: SOC2-extract.pdf (requested by Rajiv on call), network-topology.png (diagram we referenced).

Thanks,
Jordan
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
From: Elena Martinez <emartinez@finsecure.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Patel <rpatel@finsecure.com>, security@finsecure.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 14:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + ask: deployment mode & data custody clarifications

Jordan — thanks, useful summary. A few clarifications from security:  

- Physical isolation preference: For cardholder data scope (our PCI environment) we require dedicated hosts (no multi-tenant GPUs) for prod. For lower-sensitivity workloads (research/staging) logical isolation + encryption is acceptable.
- BYOK: required for all environments. Keys must be under our KMS (we can provide AWS KMS ARNs or an on-prem HSM connector).
- Control plane: management metadata and audit logs must be stored in a US region (we cannot have control metadata transit or be stored in EU/APAC).  
- Network: Prod inference nodes must not have outbound internet access; outbound to Redwood control plane endpoints over a customer-managed VPN is acceptable.

Can Nikhil map those controls to Redwood27s deployment options and highlight where a Private on-prem deployment is the only path vs Dedicated Reserved capacity? Also share a short list of evidence we can hand to our auditors (certificate names, log formats, retention guarantees).

Elena
Director, Security & Compliance | FinSecure
emartinez@finsecure.com
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <emartinez@finsecure.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + ask: deployment mode & data custody clarifications — tech mapping

Elena, Rajiv — thanks for the clear points. Below is a short technical mapping between your asks and our deployment modes, with gaps called out.

1) Physical host isolation (Prod PCI):
- Dedicated capacity (Redwood Dedicated): provides GPU pool reservation and tenant isolation at the orchestration layer. However, on many cloud providers GPUs are still shared at the host level unless you select provider27s dedicated hosts (additional cost). If your policy mandates physical single-tenant hosts we recommend Private deployment on customer-owned or dedicated-hosts in a cloud account you control (we can support AWS Dedicated Hosts or an on-prem appliance).

2) BYOK for keys and payloads:
- Supported in Private and Dedicated. For Hosted API, BYOK is limited (we manage key lifecycle). We can integrate with AWS KMS ARNs or HSM via our private control plane for Private deployments. We'll include key-rotation windows and envelope encryption details in the doc.

3) Control plane residency and audit logs:
- Private: control plane and logs can be fully contained in your VPC/region — meets the US-only requirement.
- Dedicated: logs can be forwarded into your logging endpoints; however, some control metadata (for multi-tenant controller services) may still transit Redwood control-plane endpoints unless you run Dedicated with private control-plane routing. We'll document exact fields and retention guarantees.

4) Network egress restrictions:
- Private (VPC/on-prem): inference nodes can be configured with no public internet egress; outbound allowed only to customer-managed endpoints (VPN/Direct Connect).
- Dedicated: typically requires a managed egress path; we can create strict egress rules but may still use Redwood-managed orchestration endpoints unless a private-control-plane option is provisioned.

Evidence list we will provide (first pass):
- SOC 2 report extract (scope + relevant controls) — SOC2-extract.pdf
- KMS integration guide (BYOK flow) — will attach
- Audit log schema & retention SLA summary — will attach
- Network topology sample & recommended ACLs — network-topology.png

I27ll assemble a short technical appendix and a matrix (controls vs deployment modes) and share by EOD Thursday. If helpful, I can also join your internal security review next Tuesday.

—Nikhil
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
nikhil_sharma@redwood.com

4) If confirmed, schedule a 60-min security deep-dive with your infra team — propose Tue 6/22 or Wed 6/23.
